why: Registered after the Llama-3.1 k=4 (layer 18) steering result was seen: H1 inconclusive, no length shift. At layer 18 Llama's mean (B - C) direction holds 26% of the pair-gap energy, against 59% at Qwen layer 16; the shared share is far higher at shallower depth (Llama layer 9: 70%). The earlier Qwen layer-wise decomposition (exploratory) had already suggested shallow layers carry the cleanest shared format signal. This follow-up tests the same hypotheses at depth k = 2 (round(L * 2 / 7)). It is a new, separately registered test, not a replacement of the k = 4 results, which stand as registered.
reuse: everything except the steered conditions comes from the finished replication run of the same model: admitted histories, baseline B and C answers (teacher-forcing references), fold assignment, regenerated open-unit histories and their B and C answers. Prompts are rebuilt and must match the registered prompt lengths.
vectors: cross-fitted mean ordinary (B - C) at depth k = 2 over the run's own folds (v2.1-style units); full-sample mean at k = 2 for the open units; random Gaussian controls scaled to the matching mean norm (seeds above)
models: llama31 and gemma2 after their replication runs; qwen25 after a replication run of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct through the same registered pipeline (replication/run.py, family qwen25, model files pinned by intervention/protocol.json), which also gives a same-pipeline k = 4 reference for Qwen

primary.per_model: two hypotheses per model at depth k = 2, each with two-sided 97.5% history-cluster bootstrap intervals (4000 resamples, numpy seed 453)
primary.H1s_length_v21: ordinary v2.1-style units: L_sign = mean log n(C_plus_mean) - log n(C_minus_mean) and L_random = mean log n(C_plus_mean) - log n(C_plus_random); replicates if both lower bounds > 0; absent if L_sign inside [-0.05, 0.05]; otherwise inconclusive
primary.H2s_length_open: the same on the open units

secondary: S_random, S_sign and gap closed at k = 2
comparison with k = 4 on the same units
not_claimed: Choosing k = 2 after seeing a k = 4 null is disclosed here; k = 2 results are a registered follow-up, and the k = 4 outcomes remain the primary replication results.
